narrative: Material PL1__MCE911A1 shows stable, continuous variable demand averaging 297 units/day with no trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=1.04), making the combined-variance safety stock formula critical. The EOQ of 2,971 units dramatically reduces order frequency from 321 to 25 orders/year, while the data-driven safety stock of 936 units (down from 1,956) correctly reflects actual lead-time and demand risk at 95% service level. Storage utilisation of 77.1% confirms the policy is feasible within capacity.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous daily demand with high volume makes a continuous-review fixed-reorder-point policy optimal. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs; the (r,Q) structure responds immediately when stock hits the reorder point, which is essential given unstable lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Lead-time CV exceeds 1.0 — the dominant risk is transport variability (60% of variance). If lead times lengthen structurally, sigma_ltd and safety stock will need upward revision.
